features.title: Manage persistent agents
features.summary: Create, edit, enable and remove agents — handle, name, glyph, description, instructions, Agent preset, model route and reasoning effort — from one Host-owned registry every browser and agent reads. A built-in @dsh agent ships with the harness defaults and cannot be deleted.
failureModes: A handle is a slug; a name alone is enough to create one.
Removing the built-in @dsh agent is refused and reported.
Removing an already-removed agent reports it as missing.
A save past the 100-agent limit is reported and existing agents stay.

verification.testName: the built-in agent pins nothing, so it means the harness default
saves a new agent with usage metadata and keeps it on update
seeds the built-in agent and keeps it out of deletion
a scope prefix lists agents only

features.title: Mention an agent where a thread starts
features.summary: A leading @handle dispatches an ordinary thread on that agent: its preset, its model route, its instructions and the user's text as the opening prompt. The @ menu lists enabled agents, @agent:/@a: narrows it, and another source's scope stays empty.
failureModes: An unknown handle stays a plain comment.
A disabled agent is not offered and does not dispatch.
A catalog without the agent's route leaves the Host default model.

verification.testName: the opening message names the agent and carries the prompt
decodes the Host catalog into routable rows and the default key
another source scope leaves this source empty
